caption: One furnace: the hopper under the input chest drops items into the furnace's top, the hopper under the fuel chest pushes coal into its side, and the hopper under the furnace takes each result down into the output chest.

Two furnaces sharing one input chest and one fuel chest: the items bounce between the two hoppers above the furnaces, and a small clock (two hoppers passing two swords) keeps both furnaces powered, which holds every hopper touching them still; every 65 ticks it lets go for 2 ticks, and each furnace takes one item and one coal and gives one result.

Three furnaces sharing one input chest and one fuel chest: the items circle a ring of six hoppers above the furnaces, and a small clock (two hoppers passing two swords) keeps all three furnaces powered, which holds every hopper touching them still; every 65 ticks it lets go for 2 ticks, and each furnace takes one item and one coal and gives one result.

Four furnaces sharing one input chest and one fuel chest: the items circle a ring of eight hoppers above the furnaces, and a small clock (two hoppers passing two swords) keeps all four furnaces powered, which holds every hopper touching them still; every 65 ticks it lets go for 2 ticks, and each furnace takes one item and one coal and gives one result.

Two furnaces per slice, as many slices side by side as you need: the items circle a ring of hoppers above the furnaces and the coal a second ring beside them; a small clock lets each furnace's top hopper take one item every 12 seconds and two slower clocks let its side hopper take one coal every half minute, so every furnace gets an even share. The end pieces hold the chests, the clocks and the turns of the rings.

The same slice as smelter-row (two furnaces, 14 blocks a furnace) with small end pieces: both rings turn right at the ends of the row, so they stay short. A small clock lets each furnace's top hopper take one item every 10 seconds; a second clock, slower and starting late, lets each side hopper take one coal every 41 seconds, once the coal has filled its ring.

A narrower slice, 12 blocks a furnace: the two furnaces stand four apart with their coal hoppers on the inner faces, so one block between those hoppers locks both, and the repeaters that lock the item hoppers stand on the coal ring. Both rings turn just past the row's ends; a small clock lets each furnace take one item every 10 seconds and a slower clock one coal every 36 seconds.

Eight furnaces fed by one hopper line, each taking exactly one raw ore and one coal every time the line fills up to its last hopper: that hopper's comparator unlocks all the furnace hoppers at once for a moment, so the load and the coal are shared out evenly and nothing runs once the chest is empty. Put a double chest of raw ore and 7–8 stacks of coal in, come back in 72 minutes. Variant: super-smelter-8-blast (blast furnaces: twice as fast, raw ores only).

Two 8-furnace super smelters back to back under a double chest of ore and a double chest of coal, each half feeding one row: every furnace takes exactly one raw ore and one coal each time its row's hopper line fills up, so all 16 furnaces work from the start and nothing runs once the chest is empty. Put a double chest of raw ore and 7–8 stacks of coal in, come back in 36 minutes. Variant: super-smelter-16-blast (blast furnaces: twice as fast, raw ores only).
The 8-furnace super smelter built with blast furnaces: twice as fast, but blast furnaces only take raw ores. Put a double chest of raw ore and 7–8 stacks of coal in, come back in 36 minutes.

The 16-furnace super smelter built with blast furnaces: twice as fast, but blast furnaces only take raw ores (each row has its own output line: one hopper line could not carry 16 blast furnaces' ingots). Put a double chest of raw ore and 7–8 stacks of coal in, come back in 18 minutes.
